98	// ── Wave builder (Kahn's algorithm) ──────────────────────────────────────────
99	
100	function buildWaves(lanePlan) {
101	  const lanes = lanePlan.lanes
102	  const ids = Object.keys(lanes)
103	  const inDeg = {}
104	  const adj = {}
105	
106	  for (const id of ids) {
107	    const deps = lanes[id].depends_on || []
108	    for (const dep of deps) {
109	      if (!lanes[dep]) throw new Error(`Task '${id}' depends on '${dep}', which does not exist in the lane plan`)
110	    }
111	    inDeg[id] = deps.length
112	    for (const dep of deps) {
113	      ;(adj[dep] = adj[dep] || []).push(id)
114	    }
115	  }
116	
117	  const waves = []
118	  let queue = ids.filter(id => inDeg[id] === 0).sort()
119	
120	  while (queue.length > 0) {
121	    waves.push([...queue])
122	    const next = []
123	    for (const id of queue) {
124	      for (const child of adj[id] || []) {
125	        inDeg[child]--
126	        if (inDeg[child] === 0) next.push(child)
127	      }
128	    }
129	    queue = next.sort()
130	  }
131	
132	  const placed = new Set(waves.flat())
133	  const cyclic = ids.filter(id => !placed.has(id))
134	  if (cyclic.length > 0) throw new Error(`Cyclic dependency detected among tasks: ${cyclic.sort().join(', ')}`)
135	
136	  return waves
137	}

139	// ── File classification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

141	function classifyFiles(files) {
142	  const isTest = f => {
143	    const base = f.split('/').pop()
144	    return base.startsWith('test_') || base.endsWith('_test.py') ||
145	      base.endsWith('.test.ts') || base.endsWith('.test.js') ||
146	      base.endsWith('.spec.ts') || base.endsWith('.spec.js') ||
147	      base.endsWith('_test.go') || base.endsWith('Tests.swift') ||
148	      f.includes('/tests/') || f.includes('/Tests/') ||
149	      base === 'conftest.py'
150	  }
151	  const testFiles = (files || []).filter(isTest)
152	  const implFiles = (files || []).filter(f => !isTest(f))
153	  return { testFiles, implFiles }
154	}

156	// ── Text-to-JSON parser for datum-cli agents ───────────────────────────────
157	
158	function parseAgentJson(text, fallback) {
159	  if (!text || typeof text !== 'string') return fallback || null
160	  const cleaned = text.replace(/```[a-z]*\n?/g, '').trim()
161	  const start = cleaned.search(/[{[]/)
162	  const end = Math.max(cleaned.lastIndexOf('}'), cleaned.lastIndexOf(']'))
163	  if (start === -1 || end === -1) return fallback || null
164	  try { return JSON.parse(cleaned.slice(start, end + 1)) }
165	  catch { return fallback || null }
166	}

168	// ── Lane context shell command builder ─────────────────────────────────────

170	function laneCtxCmd(packet, wt) {
171	  const ctx = JSON.stringify({
172	    task_id: packet.task_id,
173	    stage: packet.stage,
174	    allowed_write_files: packet.allowed_write_files,
175	    forbidden_write_files: packet.forbidden_write_files,
176	    commit_prefix: packet.commit_prefix,

180	}
181	
182	// ── JSON packet builder ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
183	
184	function buildPacket(taskId, testFiles, implFiles, lane, wt, cfg, stage, extras) {
185	  return {
186	    schema_version: '1.0',
187	    task_id: taskId,
188	    stage,
189	    title: lane.title,
190	    working_directory: wt,
191	    test_command: cfg.testCommand,
192	    acceptance_criteria: lane.acceptance_criteria || [],
193	    red_note: lane.red_note || '',
194	    allowed_write_files: stage === 'RED' ? testFiles
195	      : stage === 'GREEN' ? implFiles
196	      : [...testFiles, ...implFiles],
197	    forbidden_write_files: stage === 'RED' ? implFiles
198	      : stage === 'GREEN' ? testFiles
199	      : [],
200	    commit_prefix: stage === 'RED' ? `red(${taskId})`
201	      : stage === 'GREEN' ? `green(${taskId})`
202	      : `refactor(${taskId})`,
203	    ...extras,
204	  }
205	}

207	// ── Per-lane TDD saga ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

209	async function runLane(taskId, lanePlan, worktreePaths, cfg) {
210	  const lane = lanePlan.lanes[taskId]
211	  const wt = worktreePaths[taskId]
212	  const isStructural = lane.stage === 'structural'
213	
214	  // #5: compute once per lane
215	  const { testFiles, implFiles } = classifyFiles(lane.files)
216	  const acStr = (lane.acceptance_criteria || []).join('\n')
217	
218	  // Per-lane test command: only run THIS lane's test files, not the global set
219	  const laneTestCmd = testFiles.length > 0
220	    ? `uv run pytest ${testFiles.join(' ')} -x -q`
221	    : cfg.testCommand

225

228	    if (!r) return { task_id: taskId, status: 'failed', stage: 'REFACTOR', error: 'refactor failed' }
229	    return { task_id: taskId, status: 'completed' }

232	  // ── Skeleton preflight (E2: capture output directly, no separate read agent) ──
233	  const skeletonText = await agent(

235	    `--tasks ${cfg.lanePlanPath} --output .datum/runs/${cfg.runId}/preflight-${taskId}.json 2>&1`,

501	    log(`[${taskId}] REFACTOR: skipped (${(preCheck && preCheck.reason) || 'nothing to improve'})`)

505	  log(`[${taskId}] REFACTOR: proceeding (${preCheck.reason})`)
506

509	
510	  const refactor = await agent(
511	    `SETUP (run first): ${refactorCtxCmd}\n` +

514	  )

516	  if (!refactor) {

518	    return null
519	  }
520	  if (!refactor.committed && refactor.failure_reason && !refactor.failure_reason.toLowerCase().includes('nothing to')) {
521	    log(`[${taskId}] REFACTOR FAILED: ${refactor.failure_reason}`)

526	    return { verified: true }
527	  }
528	
529	  const checkText = await agent(
530	    `cd "${wt}" && datum verify-stage green --repo "${wt}" --test-command "${laneCfg.testCommand}"\nReturn ONLY the JSON output, nothing else.`,
531	    { label: `verify-refactor:${taskId}`, phase: 'Act', model: 'haiku' }
532	  )
533	  const check = parseAgentJson(checkText, { verified: false })
534	
535	  if (!check || !check.verified) {

544	const a = (typeof args === 'string') ? JSON.parse(args) : (args || {})

572	}

574	// ── Auto-partition: group waves into batches of ≤5 tasks ────────────────
575	
576	const MAX_BATCH = 5
577	
578	// Split oversized waves — intra-wave tasks are independent, so splitting is safe
579	const splitWaves = []
580	for (const wave of waves) {
581	  if (wave.length <= MAX_BATCH) {
582	    splitWaves.push(wave)

595	    batches.push(curBatch)

597	    curCount = 0

602	if (curBatch.length > 0) batches.push(curBatch)

612

631	    { label: `root-wt${batchTag}`, phase: 'Setup', model: 'haiku' }
632	  )

640	    { label: `setup-wt${batchTag}`, phase: 'Setup', model: 'haiku' }
641	  )

643

648	  // Write once to root, then cp to lanes (avoids N× JSON inline in shell command)

message.content: does local git have task ids? like TASK-0001 is it a built in feature?

content.text:
No, Git has no built-in task/ticket ID system. Commit messages, branches, and tags are freestrings — any `TASK-0001` pattern you see is a convention enforced by the team or tooling (Jira prefixes, Linear IDs, etc.), not something Git tracks or validates natively.

The closest built-in concepts are:
- **Commit SHA** — the actual unique identifier Git uses
- **`git notes`** — lets you attach metadata to commits after the fact, but nobody uses it for task tracking

If you want enforced task IDs on commits, that's a `commit-msg` hook or a tool like datum's `commit_prefix` in the lane context. Want me to wire something up?

content.text:
Yes. GitHub sub-issues are just regular issues with a parent link. Every sub-issue gets its own `#number` — `#201`, `#202`, etc. There's no separate ID system; they're first-class issues that happen to have a parent.

So the wireframe is accurate — `#201` is both the sub-issue ID and the lane ID. Commits would literally say `red(#201)`, `green(#201)`.

This means the decomposition must happen **within the single file** using code organization, or via `workflow()` calls to separate named workflows. True multi-file module extraction is not possible.

---

## 2. What Is Extractable (Pure Logic)

These functions are pure -- data in, data out, no side effects, no `agent()` / `log()` calls:

| Function | Lines | Tier | Line Count | Unit-Testable Today? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `buildWaves(lanePlan)` | L100-L137 | Logic | 38 | Yes -- Kahn's algorithm, throws on cycles |
| `classifyFiles(files)` | L141-L154 | Logic | 14 | Yes -- regex matching, no I/O |
| `parseAgentJson(text, fallback)` | L158-L166 | Logic | 9 | Yes -- string parsing |
| `laneCtxCmd(packet, wt)` | L170-L180 | Logic | 11 | Yes -- builds a shell string |
| `buildPacket(taskId, ...)` | L184-L205 | Logic | 22 | Yes -- object construction |
| Contract extraction (inline in `runLane`) | L339-L352 | Logic | 14 | Yes if extracted -- regex + filter |

Total pure logic: ~108 lines. These could be in a shared file if imports were supported, but they cannot be.

The 6 schemas (L31-L96) are pure data: **66 lines**.

---

## 3. What Has Mixed Tiers

`runLane()` (L209-L521, **313 lines**) is the biggest problem. It mixes:
- **Logic**: `classifyFiles()` call (L215), `contractSummary` extraction (L339-L352), skeptic cross-validation (L480-L484), file ownership check (L506-L511)
- **Data/Infra**: every `agent()` call (RED, GREEN, verify, reflect, skeptic, refactor), `parallel()` calls
- **Presentation**: 30+ `log()` calls for progress reporting

`runRefactor()` (L524-L580, **57 lines**) is similarly mixed but smaller.

The main body (L582-L899, **318 lines**) is mostly Data/Infra orchestration (Setup, Merge, Cleanup phases) with Presentation (logging).

---

## 4. Concrete Proposal

Given the no-import constraint, I propose **two strategies** in priority order:

### Strategy A: Inline Reorganization (works today, no runtime risk)

Reorganize the single file into clearly delimited sections with section headers. This doesn't hit DPS-103's 500-line cap, but it establishes the tier boundaries for when imports become available.

```
// ══ TIER: SCHEMAS (pure data) ══════════════════════════
// Lines 31-96: all 6 schemas

// ══ TIER: LOGIC (pure functions, zero side effects) ════
// buildWaves, classifyFiles, parseAgentJson, laneCtxCmd, buildPacket
// + extracted: extractContractSummary, crossValidateBugs, checkFileOwnership

// ══ TIER: ORCHESTRATION (agent calls, git ops) ═════════
// runLane, runRefactor

// ══ TIER: MAIN (phase flow, batch loop) ════════════════
// Topology, batch loop (Setup/Act/Merge/Cleanup), Docs, Triage
```

**Specific extractions from `runLane()`:**

1. **`extractContractSummary(acceptanceCriteria)`** -- pull L338-L352 into a standalone function. Currently inline. Pure logic, 15 lines, trivially testable.

2. **`crossValidateBugs(skepticResults, lenses)`** -- pull L469-L503 (the skeptic consensus logic) into a function. Returns `{ allBugs, brokenCount, crossValidated }`. Pure logic, 35 lines.

3. **`checkFileOwnership(testFiles, implFiles, stageResults)`** -- pull L506-L511 into a function returning violations array. Pure logic, 6 lines.

This brings the pure-logic section to ~160 lines and reduces `runLane()` from 313 to ~255 lines.

### Strategy B: Sub-Workflow Composition (larger split, more risk)

Split into two workflow files:

**File 1: `skills/datum-tdd-act.js`** (~480 lines) -- the orchestrator
- `meta` export
- All schemas
- All pure logic functions
- Main body: Topology, batch loop, Docs, Triage phases
- `runRefactor()` stays here (57 lines, not worth a separate workflow)

**File 2: `skills/datum-tdd-lane.js`** (~400 lines) -- the lane saga
- Its own `meta` export
- `runLane()` reimplemented as a standalone workflow accepting `{ taskId, lanePlan, worktreePath, cfg }` as `args`
- Invoked from the orchestrator as: `await workflow("datum-tdd-lane", { taskId, lanePlan, worktreePaths, cfg })`

This hits the 500-line cap for both files. But there are significant risks:
- **`workflow()` calls may not support returning structured results** the way `runLane()` currently returns `{ task_id, status, stage, error }`. Need to verify the `workflow()` return contract.
- **The DAG scheduler (L696-L728) uses `Promise` resolvers** for dependency gating across lanes. If each lane is a separate workflow, the DAG coordination mechanism needs rethinking -- you can't share `depPromises` closures across `workflow()` boundaries.
- **Resume semantics change**: a separate workflow has its own journaling scope, so partial resume behavior may differ.

---

## 5. Schema Placement

The 6 schemas total 66 lines. They should stay in the orchestrator file regardless of strategy. They're referenced by `{ schema: STAGE_RESULT_SCHEMA }` in `agent()` options -- if lane execution moves to a sub-workflow, that sub-workflow needs its own copy (since no imports). Duplication is the cost.

If the runtime ever supports imports, schemas move to `skills/datum-tdd-schemas.js`.

---

## 6. Prompt Templates

The agent prompts are currently inline strings in `runLane()`. Extracting them to named constants (e.g., `RED_PROMPT_TEMPLATE`, `GREEN_PROMPT_TEMPLATE`) is **worth doing**:

- **Pro**: makes `runLane()` shorter by ~60 lines, makes prompts auditable in one place, eases prompt iteration without hunting through control flow
- **Con**: templates need interpolation (working dir, packet JSON, etc.), so they'd need to be functions: `const redPrompt = (ctxCmd, packetStr) => \`...\``
- **Verdict**: Extract as template functions at the top of the file, right after schemas. Low risk, high readability gain.

---

## 7. Recommended Priority Order

1. **Extract `extractContractSummary()`** -- inline logic buried in `runLane()`, easy win, immediately testable. (15 min)

2. **Extract `crossValidateBugs()`** -- the skeptic consensus block is complex enough to deserve its own function with unit tests. (15 min)

3. **Extract prompt template functions** -- 5-6 template functions, reduces `runLane()` by ~60 lines. (30 min)

4. **Reorganize file with tier section headers** -- cosmetic but establishes the boundary for future splits. (10 min)

5. **Evaluate `workflow()` return contract** -- before attempting Strategy B, verify that `await workflow("name", args)` returns the workflow's `return` value. If it does, proceed to split. If it doesn't, Strategy B is blocked.

6. **Split `runLane` into sub-workflow** (Strategy B) -- only after step 5 confirms feasibility and after finding a DAG coordination pattern that works across workflow boundaries.

---

## 8. Migration Risk Summary

| Change | Risk | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Extract pure functions (within file) | Near zero | Same file, same scope, no runtime change |
| Extract prompt templates | Low | String interpolation refactor, testable |
| Tier section headers | Zero | Comments only |
| Sub-workflow split | **Medium-High** | DAG Promise coordination breaks, resume semantics change, return value contract unclear, schema duplication |

---

## 9. Minimum Split to Hit DPS-103 (500 Lines)

The file is 899 lines. To get under 500, you need to remove ~400 lines. The only viable cut is extracting `runLane()` (313 lines) + `runRefactor()` (57 lines) + the schemas they reference (66 lines if duplicated) into a sub-workflow. That gets the orchestrator to ~460 lines and the lane workflow to ~440 lines.

But this is blocked by the DAG coordination problem described above. The practical path is:

1. Do steps 1-4 from the priority list (gets the file more readable but still ~800 lines)
2. Accept the DPS-103 violation with an explicit waiver comment explaining the runtime constraint
3. Revisit when/if Claude Code adds `import` support to workflows

The 500-line cap exists to prevent tangled files. This file is long but not tangled -- each function has a clear boundary. The right response to DPS-103 here is a documented exception, not a forced split that breaks the DAG scheduler.</result>

- `.catch()` on `runLane()` — no more deadlocks on crash

- **Worktree isolation enforcement** — agents must `cd` into their worktree AND commit there. The `lane-context.json` has `working_directory` but nothing prevents the agent from wandering. - **Idempotent worktree setup** — `datum worktrees setup` needs to detect existing dirty worktrees and reset them cleanly on resume.
- **Duplicate commit detection** — verify-green should check if a green commit already exists before allowing the GREEN agent to run.

Want me to file these as GH issues, or tackle the worktree isolation enforcement now since it's the root cause of most of these failures?
